## Overview
<!--
At a high-level address what your proposal is and how it will address
the problem identified. Highlight any benefits to the R Community that
follow from solving the problem. This should be your most compelling
section.

Include concrete actions you will take and estimated timeline.

This proposal is for an R package which wraps Vale, together with a Vale style written for R package documentation, so that documentation can be linted from R, on the command line and on CI.
It lints both the external documentation of a package, its vignettes and READMEs, and the comments in its R source files, including the roxygen comments from which help pages are generated, and reports the file, line, rule and a message explaining what was wrong, as a data frame in R or as JSON for AI tools and CI reporting.

Vale already provides rules for sentence length, readability scores, and words often reported by readers as condescending like "simply", "just" and "obviously", spread across several existing styles and tuned for general prose.
The work in this project is to select the subset of those rules that make sense for R package documentation, set their thresholds by running them over real packages so that they aren't noisy out of the box, and add a vocabulary of common R terms.
Together these form a default style that ships with the package and is also published for people who use Vale directly.
Rules are configured from a Vale config file at the package root, which the package can generate, so that users can adjust the defaults according to taste.

Building on Vale keeps the amount of novel code small.
Vale handles extracting comments from R files, parsing Markdown, running rules and integrating with editors, and its rules are defined as data rather than code, so the community can contribute rules without needing to write R.
The package itself has three parts: locating an existing Vale binary or downloading one for the user's platform when asked, following the pattern used by blogdown and tinytex; the style; and the R interface, config generation and GitHub Action.

The main dependency is Vale itself, which is actively maintained and publishes binaries for Linux, macOS and Windows on every release.
Nothing requires a service or a paid account, so there are no ongoing costs.
